identity.name: Chronomètre à Résonance
identity.one_liner: Two independent balance wheels regulating each other through resonance rather than a shared gear train, shown on a twin-dial layout that displays two time zones.

comps.condition: Souscription No. 007, an early founding-client edition, not the standard RS
Platinum RN, a different reference owned by Francis Ford Coppola

provenance_events.description: A Souscription-series Chronomètre à Résonance, No. 007 of the original 20-piece founding-client edition from circa 2000, sold for $13,922,000 at Phillips New York Watch Auction XIV, the highest price ever paid at commercial auction for a 21st-century wristwatch and for any watch by an independent watchmaker.

provenance_events.person_or_event: One-off Résonance at a charity gala
provenance_events.description: A unique Résonance, serial 638-RQ, raised SGD 4 million for the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation. A charity result for a one-off watch is not a resale comparison for the RS.

narrative.story: The Résonance was one of the first watches F.P. Journe produced under his own name, a subscription series of twenty pieces offered to founding clients around 2000 to help finance the fledgling company before it built the boutique network that supports it today. The mechanical premise is unusual: two separate balance wheels, each with its own escapement, are placed close enough together that they entrain each other through physical resonance, a phenomenon Journe used to improve rate stability rather than just as a display gimmick. The dial's twin sub-dials read two time zones, one for each balance train.
narrative.collector_notes: Souscription-series pieces from the original circa-2000 run are a distinct, far scarcer population than the standard-production Résonance that followed; collectors treat them as effectively a different watch for valuation purposes despite sharing the model name.
